claim.quote: In this work, data on the interactions of a carbon-ion beam with kinetic energies of 4.0A~GeV and 4.5A~GeV with C, Al, Cu, and Pb targets are used to measure transverse momentum spectra and rapidity distributions of $\Lambda$ hyperon yields.

name: BM@N Lambda hyperon production in 4.0A and 4.5A GeV carbon-nucleus interactions
notes: Published in JHEP (August 2026) according to a search result; dated by the arXiv v1 submission.

summary.plain: BM@N measured how many Lambda hyperons, strange particles, come out of carbon-ion beams hitting carbon, aluminium, copper and lead targets at 4.0 and 4.5 GeV per nucleon, and compared the spectra with transport models and other experiments.
summary.technical: Transverse-momentum spectra and rapidity distributions of Lambda hyperon yields in C+C, C+Al, C+Cu and C+Pb at 4.0A and 4.5A GeV, compared with DCM-SMM, UrQMD and PHSD predictions and with Lambda measurements at similar energies; the first fixed-target experiment at the NICA complex.

title: Production of Lambda hyperons in 4.0A GeV and 4.5A GeV carbon-nucleus interactions at the Nuclotron
why_it_matters: Strangeness production just above threshold is sensitive to the equation of state of dense nuclear matter that BM@N and the future CBM and NICA experiments study.
